chunk_map.heading: H1 + lede (Map the gaps, read your stack)
Phase 1: Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps
Read the contrast, push back where it generalises
Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed
Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule
Phase 2: Find the work you repeat across your stack
Scan your history for the work that recurs
Draw your top work-shapes as diagrams
Sidestep: check your menu against the field's
Decide what crosses back to your main repo

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 8 "Sidestep: check your menu against the field's": line 89 (current wording): "The shapes stay in this session's scrollback; you build the handoff prompt from them." Ruling on the carve-out question: this exercise is included by the module file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md (verified via the include link at that file's line 37, `[Spot gaps, build the loop](exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md)`). Its `## What You'll Learn` (line 12) precedes that include in file order, and its fifth bullet (line 19) reads: "**Generalize** the shapes you mapped into a handoff prompt that builds your workflow skills across your stack" — introducing "a handoff prompt" as named vocabulary before the exercise's own chunks render. `check_slides.md` §1's fourth carve-out states verbatim that vocabulary the enclosing module file's signposting introduces (its own example: "the test-strategy skill" named in What You'll Learn) counts as prior context for the exercises it includes, and that module include-order is deck order. The pattern here is structurally identical to the compendium's own worked example: an indefinite-then-definite noun pair (WYL's "a handoff prompt" → exercise's "the handoff prompt"), same section (`## What You'll Learn`), same relation (enclosing module → included exercise). The carve-out does not require the WYL bullet to use the definite article — it requires only that the module's signposting name the term, which bullet 5 does directly ("a handoff prompt"). Ruling: the carve-out covers "the handoff prompt" here. This is not a borderline read of the carve-out; it is the carve-out's stated shape applied to a second, matching instance. No REVISE.

Re-checked against current wording. The maintainer's accepted fix removed the positional pointer entirely: line 89 now reads "...you build the handoff prompt from them," with no forward reference to "the close" or any other file-by-position. Scanned the rest of chunk 8 and the whole body for any remaining cross-file positional pointer — none found. The prior REVISE's target string is gone and no replacement positional callback was introduced in its place.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No "the X you did/saw" backward callbacks to a specific prior exercise/lecture beat appear in the body. Chunk 0's references to "the M5 session" / "the M5 worktree" point at the prior module's artefact (verified present: curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md produces the M5 worktree and its `m5/<slug>` branch, per that module's own artefact contract), not a missing beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-then-reveal demo beat in this file — every prompt asks Claude to analyze/produce, with no guess-before-outcome structure.

Every chunk carries a self-carrying instructional or informational claim (e.g. chunk 4 "Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule" gives two concrete push-back conditions; chunk 9 "Decide what crosses back to your main repo" states the worktree-vs-main-repo split as a standalone claim). None reduces to a bare wait-state bullet.

Checked each header against its chunk body under sequential read; closest case remains chunk 8 "Sidestep: check your menu against the field's" whose body (menu-of-primitives prompt + "Expect the list to look familiar" + the What-happened recap, now ending on the handoff-prompt line) still centers on comparing the student's own checks against a wider field menu — header holds.

Scanned body prose (fenced Prompt blocks exempted). No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction, no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlative (closest: "two runs are enough to place every lesson" in chunk 0 — a training claim, not a self-rating of the exercise/training's own quality, so it does not trip the value-prop-leak sub-item), no number-plus-retraction, no abstraction-noun stack, no empty-leg verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No maintainer-dialect nouns (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) in body prose. "Compound" terminology (chunk 3: "Cleaning is the compound move that keeps the loop fast") is this training's own earned arc vocabulary (module Key Concepts names "the compound ladder"; WYL bullet 2 "Cut one rule ... the diagnosis killed"), not repo-maintainer dialect, and register is AE101 engineer-IC audience where this reads as ordinary shop vocabulary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest specimens: chunk 0's five bold labels (Time/Session/What you do/What you build/The point) are the corpus-standard exercise-header template (chrome, not narrative bold) and chunk 6's two bolded blockquote leads ("Fast operator?", "Cut the scan when the top patterns are clear enough to use.") are widget/label-style callouts, which the file's own maintainer block ("Emphasis pass" note, line 99) records as deliberately untouched by the 2026-07-09 de-bolding pass. Both stay inside the carve-out; no narrative-sentence bold found elsewhere.
